title: The Balaton Ring: Seven Days Around Hungary's Inland Sea

hook: Balaton is shallow, jade-green and 77 km long, and the ring around it is flat enough that all the climbing is voluntary. This week rides the paved Balatoni Bringakör anticlockwise, then leaves it twice, over the Tihany peninsula, and into the basalt buttes and gravel lanes of the Káli basin. Fried fogas, cold Olaszrizling, reed beds full of grebes, and one short ferry that saves you forty kilometres.

snapshot.Best period: Mid-May to mid-June, or the first three weeks of September
snapshot.Start / End: Balatonfüred → Balatonfüred (loop, ~308 km ridden; the ring itself is ~204 km)
snapshot.Getting there: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD), then MÁV line 26 (Kelenföld → Balatonfüred → Tapolca, 2 h 10) north shore, or line 29 (Székesfehérvár → Siófok → Nagykanizsa) south. Hévíz-Balaton (SOB) has limited seasonal traffic.

itinerary.title: Arrival, Csopak and a shakedown
itinerary.morning: Train in, collect the bike, set it up properly, saddle height, brake reach, rack bolts. Coffee on the **Tagore sétány**, the lime-shaded Balatonfüred promenade where Tagore planted a tree in 1926.
itinerary.afternoon: East on the separated path to **Csopak**, then inland to **Jásdi Pince** or **Figula Pincészet** for Csopaki Olaszrizling, flinty and high-acid off Permian red sandstone. On to **Alsóörs** and its red-sandstone Turkish House, then back.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Kisfaludy Ház** on the hillside, terrace looking straight down the peninsula, or cheaper and better at **Baricska Csárda** below it. Mákos guba at **Bergmann Cukrászda**. Early night: tomorrow has the best climb.

itinerary.title: Tihany, the abbey, and the volcanic west
itinerary.morning: Flat path to **Tihany-rév**, then the climb in the small ring. At the top, the twin-towered **Tihanyi Bencés Apátság**, founded 1055, whose charter holds the oldest written Hungarian words. Walk Echo Hill for the **Belső-tó**, the crater lake sitting 25 m above Balaton.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Aszófő, through Örvényes, Balatonudvari and **Balatonakali**, where the path fails and road 71 begins, take the parallel village streets at Zánka and Balatonszepezd. Fogas lunch at **Révfülöp**, then 12 km under the Badacsony basalt.
itinerary.evening: Base in **Badacsony**. Climb the vineyard road to **Laposa Birtok** for Kéknyelű and Juhfark facing the water, or to **Szent Orbán Borház** higher up for dinner over the whole lake.

itinerary.title: Káli basin: gravel, basalt organs, stone seas
itinerary.morning: Off the ring. Climb through Káptalantóti to **Kővágóörs**, then gravel into the **Káli-medence**, hayfields, dry-stone walls, volcanic buttes. Stop at the **Szentbékkálla kőtenger**, a field of wind-carved sandstone blocks you can scramble on.
itinerary.afternoon: Farm track to **Salföld Major** and its grey cattle, racka sheep and buffalo, then **Kékkút**, the spring behind every Theodora bottle in Hungary. Finish at the **Hegyestű Geológiai Bemutatóhely** above Monoszló: a quarried cone whose sheared face is a wall of hexagonal basalt columns.
itinerary.evening: Eat at **Káli Art Inn** in Köveskál, or taste at **Villa Sandahl** in Kővágóörs. Descend to Badacsony with Szent György-hegy (415 m) and Csobánc (376 m) black against the sky.

itinerary.title: Szigliget, Kis-Balaton and the Festetics
itinerary.morning: Leave the bikes below **Szigliget** and walk 20 minutes to **Szigligeti Vár**, the 13th-century castle that never fell to the Ottomans and owns the western basin view. Down for the flat run to Balatonederics.
itinerary.afternoon: Packed limestone past **Fenékpuszta**, where the Zala leaves the **Kis-Balaton** marshes, spoonbills, purple herons, hundreds of great white egrets in September. Into **Keszthely** on the lakefront path.
itinerary.evening: The **Festetics-kastély**, 101 rooms and a 90,000-volume Helikon Library, is the best interior on the lake. Dinner at **Bacchus Étterem**. If legs allow, spin 5 km to **Hévíz** and float on the 33-36 °C thermal lake.

itinerary.title: South shore, sphere lookout, and Kistücsök
itinerary.morning: South to **Balatonberény**, where the path leaves road 71 for good and runs flat behind the reeds. Balatonmáriafürdő, Balatonfenyves and the kisvasút crossings, the fastest 25 km of the week, and a tailwind leg in the usual north-westerly.
itinerary.afternoon: Ramp up to **Fonyód**'s Bélatelep villa terrace for the postcard of Badacsony and Szigliget across the water, then **Balatonboglár** and the 1960s concrete **Gömbkilátó** on Várdomb, before dropping to Balatonlelle and **Konyári Pincészet** for the south shore's most serious red.
itinerary.evening: Sleep in **Balatonszemes** and eat at **Kistücsök**, thirty years the best restaurant on Balaton, built around the lake's own fish and Somogy's growers, book ahead. Natural wine afterwards at **Bakos Bar**, a few doors along.

itinerary.title: Szántód, the ferry, back to the north
itinerary.morning: Easy path through **Balatonszárszó**, pause at the József Attila memorial, where the poet died in 1937, then Balatonföldvár and **Zamárdi**, with the Szamárkő boulder above the village for one more climb.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Szántód-Tihany car ferry**, BAHART's crossing of the lake's narrowest point (~1.5 km), takes seven minutes, runs year-round and carries bikes without fuss, 1,000 HUF for the passenger and 400 HUF for the bike, so about €3.50 (1,400 HUF) all in, with under-14s free and a car at 3,100 HUF (BAHART tariff from 1 June 2026). It trades the dull 40 km Siófok arm for the best short boat ride in Hungary.
itinerary.evening: Climb from Tihany-rév to the village once more in evening light, then coast to **Balatonfüred**. Dinner at **Vitorlás Étterem** by the Round Church, then out along the pier as the yacht club boats come in.

itinerary.title: The eastern arm, and out
itinerary.morning: East to **Alsóörs**, then the short inland ramp to **Felsőörs** and its 13th-century Romanesque provost's church, the finest small church on the lake and almost always empty.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to **Balatonalmádi**, up to the **Óvári kilátó** for the last panorama, then the Wesselényi beach for a swim: still around 20 °C in September.
itinerary.evening: Return the bike, then the train from Balatonalmádi or Balatonfüred. With three spare hours, ride the extra 12 km to Balatonkenese and Balatonfűzfő and close the ring by wheel rather than by ferry.

accommodationStrategy.name: Blaha Lujza Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: the actress's own 1860s villa, 200 m from the Tagore sétány and the bike path, with a courtyard where bikes lock up out of the weather. Marina, rental shop and station all walkable.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4-6 weeks ahead for May and September; 8-10 for the late-July Anna Ball week.

accommodationStrategy.name: Borbarátok Panzió
accommodationStrategy.description: a working wine house with rooms, a locked bike store, and a kitchen that will still feed you at 21:00 after the Káli day. It sits at the foot of the vineyard road, so the Laposa and Szent Orbán climb starts at the door.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3-5 weeks ahead, direct by email rather than the portals.

accommodationStrategy.name: A Balatonszemes vendégház
accommodationStrategy.description: the quiet south-shore stretch between the resort clusters, three minutes from the path and walking distance from Kistücsök, which matters after 56 km.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3-4 weeks ahead; two-night minimums are common in July-August, single nights fine in shoulder season.

logistics.connectivity: Full 4G/5G on both shores (Telekom, Yettel, One). Only the Káli-medence between Salföld and Monoszló is patchy. Carry the route offline.
logistics.emergency: 112. Hospitals in Keszthely, Siófok and Veszprém; Balatonfüred has the State Heart Hospital. Water rescue is VMSZ, via 112.
logistics.weather: The shore storm masts are not decorative. One flash per second is a first-degree warning, a fast double flash second-degree, get off the exposed north-shore road at once. Squalls arrive from the north-west in under thirty minutes with 60-80 km/h gusts.
logistics.bookingWindows: Beds 3-6 weeks in shoulder season, 8-12 for July-August. Bikes 2-3 weeks. Kistücsök and the better Badacsony cellars, 1-2 weeks.
logistics.money: Forint, roughly 390-410 HUF to €1. Cards work almost everywhere including village csárdas, but carry 15,000-20,000 HUF for the ferry kiosk, small cellars and lángos stands.
logistics.transportRules: Front and rear lights after dark and a bell are legally required. Helmets are mandatory outside built-up areas where the limit exceeds 50 km/h, which includes road 71. Cyclist alcohol tolerance is effectively zero: tastings are a lunch activity.
logistics.permits: No permit needed, but the Balaton-felvidéki Nemzeti Park confines cycling to marked forest and farm roads, stay off the single-track on Szent György-hegy and Badacsony. Kis-Balaton's inner reserve is closed; the Kányavári-sziget boardwalk is the public part.

proTips: **Ride anticlockwise.** The prevailing north-westerly pushes you along the long, fast south shore and keeps the water on your right all week.
**Roll by 08:00 in September.** Empty path, best light, and you clear road 71 under Badacsony before the wine traffic wakes.
**Treat the train as a get-out.** Every town here has a station within 300 m of the path, a headwind or a broken spoke just costs a 500 HUF kerékpárjegy.
**Take the Szántód ferry.** The Siófok arm is the ring's least interesting 40 km, and the crossing hands you Tihany from the water.
**Taste on the hill, sleep in the village.** Laposa and Szent Orbán are 150 m above Badacsonytomaj: ride up before dinner, walk down after.
**Say it right.** *"Egy pohár Kéknyelűt kérek"* gets the local grape, not the tourist Riesling; *"Van kerékpártároló?"* asks about bike storage.
**Swap Day 7 for Hévíz** if your legs are finished, floating at 33-36 °C over 38 m of peat beats 31 km of shoreline.

raw.Daily distance / gain: D1 Balatonalmádi-Csopak-Balatonfüred 29 km / +190 m. D2 Balatonfüred-Tihany-Badacsony 54 km / +430 m. D3 Káli-medence loop 57 km / +720 m. D4 Badacsony-Szigliget-Keszthely 39 km / +200 m. D5 Keszthely-Fonyód-Balatonszemes 56 km / +160 m. D6 Balatonszemes-Szántód-ferry-Balatonfüred 42 km / +280 m. D7 Balatonfüred-Alsóörs-Balatonalmádi 31 km / +260 m. Total ≈308 km / +2,240 m.
raw.Surface split: North shore ~70% dedicated asphalt path, ~25% shared low-traffic road, ~5% packed limestone at Fenékpuszta. The gaps at Balatonakali, Zánka and Badacsony-Ábrahámhegy put you on the shoulder of **road 71**, narrow and fast, the week's only real hazard. South shore ~95% separated path from Balatonberény to Siófok. The Káli day is ~45% asphalt, ~50% compacted gravel and dolomite farm track, ~5% loose basalt: 35 mm tyres minimum, 40 mm better.
raw.The Tihany climb: Flat to Tihany-rév, then ~90 m in 3.5 km at 4-6% to the Abbey terrace (village ~130 m; lake level 105 m; Csúcs-hegy 232 m, Óvár 219 m). Anticlockwise you take the gentler east flank up and the steeper west flank down to Aszófő.
raw.Rental: Balatonfüred's shops cluster around the **Tagore sétány** marina; Siófok's around **Petőfi sétány** and the Sió canal quay. Trekking bikes €10, €16/day (4,000-6,500 HUF), e-bikes €22, €30/day (9,000-12,000 HUF), weekly rates 25-35% less; panniers rarely included.
raw.Bike-friendly stays: Insist on a locked *zárható kerékpártároló*, a floor pump and breakfast from 07:30; ask for the **Kerékpárosbarát Szálláshely** designation by name.
raw.Trains with a bike (MÁV-START): Bikes ride the marked carriage on almost all Balaton regionals and fast trains on a separate **kerékpárjegy**, 500 HUF (~€1.25) for 24 hours and a single journey, with 15% off in the MÁVPlusz app; on InterCity a bike **kerékpárhelyjegy** is compulsory on top, 100-990 HUF depending on route and season, and the quota is small, so book in the app days ahead for summer weekends (2026 tariff). Lines 26 and 29 add summer bike capacity, which makes bailing out of a leg trivial.
